fixes.explanation: Bildad does not hold back. He asks Job how long he will go on saying such things, then says, "The words of your mouth are a blustering wind." (Job 8:2) That is Bildad calling Job's whole speech a gust of wind. I think that is a rough way to open.

A dripping roof is a fun picture, but it isn't what Bildad says. He says the words of Job's mouth are "…a blustering wind." (Job 8:2) That is wind, not water. I once had a leaky roof in my own bakery, and nobody called it a speech.
A heavy burden is a real thing to carry, but it isn't Bildad's word. He calls Job's words "…a blustering wind." (Job 8:2) Wind, not weight. The picture he picks is about air.
Wisdom is a fine thing to ask for. It just isn't what Bildad says here. His words are, "…ask the Almighty for mercy…" (Job 8:5) Same sentence, different request.

Bildad says the opposite. He tells Job, "Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish." (Job 8:7) So the latter days flourish, they don't shrink. Modest beginnings first, then the flourishing.

Bildad actually says the reverse. He tells Job to "…consider the discoveries of their fathers." and then says, "…we were born yesterday and know nothing…" (Job 8:8-9) So it's the fathers' discoveries he points to. The "we" are the ones who were born yesterday.

Bildad says, "While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up more quickly than grass." (Job 8:12) Even uncut, they dry up fast. That is the picture he paints. Grass isn't known for sticking around, so beating it is quite the race.

Locusts are a fair guess, but they aren't in Bildad's picture. He says the shoots "…dry up more quickly than grass." (Job 8:12) The trouble is dryness, not bugs. Nobody in this verse is eating anything.

Fear is a word you might expect, but it isn't Bildad's word here. He says, "Such is the destiny of all who forget God…" (Job 8:13) The people he is talking about are those who forget. A small word makes a big difference.
A broken cistern is a picture from another part of the Bible (Jeremiah 2:13), but Bildad doesn't use it. He says, "his security is in a spider’s web." (Job 8:14) Web, not cistern.
Right. Bildad says that if the plant is uprooted, its place "…will disown him, saying, ‘I never saw you.’" (Job 8:18) I think that is a cold goodbye. The place acts as if it never saw the plant.
Yes. Bildad says, "Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust." (Job 8:19) So others will spring from the dust. That's what the verse says, and I'll leave the rest alone.

Arguments might fit the way this talk is going, but Bildad doesn't say it. He says God "…will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy." (Job 8:21) The word is laughter. A shout of joy goes right along with it.
